faq.q: Can an NRI open a new NSC account?
faq.a: No, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are generally not eligible to open new National Savings Certificate (NSC) accounts. The scheme is designed for resident individuals.

faq.q: What happens to an NSC if I become an NRI after investing?
faq.a: If you invested in an NSC as a resident Indian and then became an NRI, your existing NSC will continue until its maturity. You cannot open a new one or renew it upon maturity.

faq.q: Can NRIs claim Section 80C benefits for NSC?
faq.a: No, NRIs cannot claim tax deductions under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act for investments in NSC, even if the investment was made when they were a resident. The deduction is available only to resident Indians.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on NSC taxable for NRIs?
faq.a: Yes, the interest earned on an NSC held by an NRI is fully taxable in India. It is usually subject to Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) at the prevailing rates.

faq.q: Where can the maturity proceeds of an NRI's NSC be credited?
faq.a: Upon maturity, the proceeds from an NRI's NSC can typically be credited to their Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account in India.

faq.q: Are there any specific rules for premature encashment of NSC for NRIs?
faq.a: The rules for premature encashment are generally the same for NRIs as for residents, allowed only under specific circumstances like the death of the account holder or a court order.
